subject: Genetics
title: Genomic Imprinting
description: Learn Genomic Imprinting in one minute.

hook.text: Some genes only work if they come from Dad. Others only if from Mom. The wrong parent's copy is silenced permanently.

buildup.text: About 100 human genes are imprinted. Methylation marks placed during egg or sperm formation silence one parent's copy.

discovery.text: The IGF2 growth gene is only read from Dad's copy. Mom's is silenced.

twist.text: Imprinting may reflect a parental conflict: Dad's genes push for bigger babies, Mom's genes restrain growth to protect.

climax.text: Imprinting errors cause diseases: Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes—both from chromosome 15, but from different parents.

punchline.text: Not just which gene—but which parent's copy matters.

quiz.question: What is genomic imprinting?
options: Genes that only work from one specific parent's copy
Mutations that only affect one gender
